assertions.name: W_is_plancherel_not_the_markov_weight
assertions.source: differs {'sym': True, 'std': True, 'alt': True}; d^2 sums to D True

description: EXPLORATORY (bean t7qv): settles the diagnosis of pyhecke.atom.nf_channel_exact so the repair decision can be made on facts, and lays out four options with blast radius. NO FIX APPLIED. The function computes chi_sym and chi_alt directly but chi_std by subtraction with W_SYM/W_STD/W_ALT, and that fails twice over. (1) Solving sum y_lam chi^lam = TR_M exactly gives y = ((q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, q^2/(q^2+1)^2, 0), consistent on all six equations and normalised, which differs from W in every component; W's numerators are d^2 for d = (q, q^2+1, q) summing to D, so W is the q-PLANCHEREL measure — a coherent object, just not the trace weight. (2) y_alt = 0, so tr_M carries no chi_alt information and the three-term inversion was wrong in SHAPE, not merely in coefficients; and y_alt = 0 is the documented Gram radical, since RADICAL is _ALT_EIG_FRAC and G.RADICAL = 0 to 1.7e-16. The standard character needs no inversion at all: chi^(2,1) = [2, h, h, -1, -1, 0] exactly, verified against direct seminormal traces at five q. RECOMMENDED option B: add _STD_CHI_FRAC and dot with it, which removes the asymmetry that caused the bug. No fit; no B_AME; nothing wired.

options.A: chi_std = (tr_M - y_sym chi_sym)/y_std; local, W_* untouched
options.C: change W_* — NOT recommended, real consumers move
options.D: leave flagged — zero call sites but exported from four modules

caveats: DIAGNOSIS ONLY — no repair is applied. The choice among A-D is a substrate decision; this probe supplies the facts, including the blast radius of option C (W_SYM/W_STD/W_ALT are consumed arithmetically by pyhecke/molecular.py lines 121/124/125, pyhecke/atom.py line 333 vertex_volume, and qou-mass/.../_internal/hecke_core.py lines 230-232).

W_SYM/W_STD/W_ALT are NOT wrong in themselves — they are the q-Plancherel measure d_lam^2/sum d^2 with d = (q, q^2+1, q). The error is using them where the Markov trace weight belongs. Any fix should leave W alone and say what it is.

Separate decision, whichever option is taken: the exact-Fraction path evaluates at _Q_FRAC = 111/100, not q_0, which is why the 1-dim channels differ from a q_0 computation in the 5th decimal. That is a design choice of the exact path, not part of this bug, but a caller wanting q_0 needs a q parameter.
